sourceInformation.artDirection: Original code-drawn, shaded pixel garden dioramas on Venus; jewel foliage and warm fruit
sourceInformation.animation: Native Blob spring rigs with continuous procedural expressions, squash, secondary leaves and antennae; distance-sampled crawler history
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-only native synthesizer music with five arrangements, effects and formant-filtered gibberish voices; separate buses; fresh music 10 percent
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub authoritative shared-world cooperation for 1-2 seats, including a non-playing host; standalone couch cooperation; no standalone internet lobby
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited headless tests allowed; one-command exact-step, ordinary-command solo/co-op and native-controller campaigns, device/pad stand-ins, workshop/storage/tuning, audio analysis, live Hub state and pristine official harness checks; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
sourceInformation.research: Original manual text and illustrated pages; downloaded a 20–40 second gameplay excerpt and inspected sampled frames: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=whykVbhZD8c . Source sound heard: unknown. Packaging page unavailable; original magazine URL returned 403.

testingFeedback: 22 distinct implementation issues were identified during automated checks and integration review; all were fixed. Test-driver timing, signed-zero and geometry assumptions are excluded.
4 critical issues: three prevented loading, starting or a usable display; one let developer invulnerability survive an unmodified retry and threatened record integrity.
The complete emulated-controller campaign: title to all 15 courses, ending, initials entry and the real saved score, using ordinary pad inputs without gameplay cheats.
Raw full-state console dumps added little compared with focused assertions and a few deliberate visual captures.
engineFeedback: The native shaded pixel rigs, synthesis, menus and exact fixed-step headless execution work together in one dependency-free engine file.
I initially assumed a custom input map inherited menu actions; it needs explicit confirm/cancel/pause/start bindings. Custom paired wraps and immediate reversal also needed authored adapters.
One authoritative graph simulation and snapshot contract for crawler history, ordered contacts, retries, co-op, workshop maps and deterministic tests.
Coordinating native input consumption, pause/menu ownership and audio lifecycle across standalone play, touch and a Hub authority without a local avatar.
Vendor engine unchanged. Authored Grid/GridMover, Arcade wake, Blob rig, native-menu layout and synth adapters add the game-specific behavior. Native portrait and TV options handle layout.
A public custom-edge hook shared by Grid, GridMover and pathfinding would simplify wrap topology and orientation.
promptFeedback: The distinctive tail-chase loop, five authored lessons and explicit device/Hub acceptance criteria made the intended finished experience clear.
The 12–18 minute human pacing target needed interpretation with the short initial tail counts. Three finite courses per garden add substance; actual first-player duration remains unknown.
Making reliable discrete planting, authoritative contacts, local device assignments, workshop topology and every menu route agree in the final single file.
Separate strict acceptance requirements from starting tuning values, and state a preferred finite-course policy for meeting the campaign pacing target.

aiHub.name: K.C.’s Hungry Hullabaloo
aiHub.description: Chomp glowing crawler tails, outwit hunting heads, and plant suspiciously scrumptious bait in five alien gardens. Share the feast in local or AI Hub co-op, then build a garden of your own.
aiHub.controls: Move: stick/D-pad, WASD/arrows or touch drag; plant: Cross/Space/context button; bites automatic; Enter confirms; Escape/Options pauses.
